tasks.short: Read applications in Recruitee against the vacancy and decide who fits the job requirements.

steps.what: Take the job order from the hiring manager and set requirements
Open each application and read CV and motivation

loop.input: CV and application form text from Recruitee
loop.output: structured candidate facts (licences, code 95, forklift/VCA certificates, years in role, shift availability, location) each with a quoted source line
loop.check: Every fact must quote a line found in the CV; facts without a quote are dropped; recruiter sees facts next to the CV
loop.stop: One pass per CV, one retry on schema error, then mark 'read manually'
loop.why_not_simpler: CVs are free text in many layouts and languages; fixed parsing misses most facts.

steps.what: Check must-haves: work permit, licences, certificates, shifts, travel distance
Judge overall fit and move candidate to a pipeline stage
Write screening notes in the candidate record

tasks.design: Configure a structured intake form in Recruitee so each vacancy has explicit must-haves and nice-to-haves. A small job on the governed HR platform pulls new applications through the Recruitee API, extracts quoted facts with a bounded model step, runs the must-have rules and writes a fact panel and a draft screening note back into Recruitee. The recruiter makes every stage move; nothing rejects automatically and there is no single match score.
tasks.previous_blocker: CVs are unstructured and vary wildly; rule-based parsers were too weak and full matching tools raised legal and works-council concerns.
tasks.enabler_now: Models can extract facts with quoted evidence reliably enough to review, and AI coding makes the Recruitee integration and rules a days-long build.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding fit for people with unusual paths, and keeping extraction errors from silently excluding candidates. Works council consent and, from 2 December 2027, high-risk AI Act duties apply.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing potential in an unusual CV and knowing what a site manager really needs beyond the written requirements.

ambition.what: Every applicant gets a must-have check within one working day of applying, instead of when the recruiter gets to the pile.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter spends less time reading and more time on intake with managers; they gain the right to sharpen must-haves per vacancy with data on why candidates fail them.

reach.task: Report on days per pipeline stage and drop-off reasons
reach.learn: Use the structured must-have data to show which requirements shrink the pool most.

reach.task: Track mandatory certificates (forklift, VCA) in Studytube
reach.learn: Hires missing a certificate can be routed to training before day one.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 builds a profile from an application and calculates a match score against vacancies.
67% of hiring leaders use AI for CV screening; 26% fear they no longer see some candidates.
No rejection may be based solely on an automated score; review must be meaningful.
CV screening tools almost always need prior works council consent.
Filtering applications becomes high-risk under the AI Act from 2 December 2027.

assumptions: Recruitee API access is available on the current plan.
Most warehouse and driver vacancies have clear must-haves (licence, certificates, shifts).
unknowns: Applications per vacancy and per month by site.
Whether the OR already has a regulation on HR software.
Whether Noordhaven uses or plans AFAS Profit 8 recruitment features.
research_questions: How many applications per month fail on a must-have, and how long does reading them take today?
On 200 past CVs, how often does extraction miss or invent a licence or certificate?
Will the works council consent to fact extraction without ranking?
Does Recruitee's own screening or questions cover the must-haves without custom code?

tasks.short: Tell candidates about duties, pay, CAO benefits, shifts and working conditions by phone, mail and in vacancy texts.

steps.what: Answer candidate questions on pay, shifts and conditions by phone and mail

loop.input: candidate question plus the vacancy info pack, CAO pay tables and site fact sheets
loop.output: draft answer citing the source paragraph
loop.check: Answer must cite a source passage; pay figures must match the CAO table lookup exactly; recruiter edits and sends
loop.stop: One draft per question; if no source matches, show 'no answer in sources' and the recruiter answers
loop.why_not_simpler: Questions arrive in free text and mixed language; a fixed FAQ covers most but not all.

steps.what: Look up CAO scale, allowances, shift pattern and site facts
Write vacancy text and candidate information

loop.input: structured vacancy fields and pay and conditions facts
loop.output: vacancy text and one-page info pack in Dutch and English
loop.check: Pay, hours and allowances are inserted from the lookup, not written by the model; recruiter approves before publishing
loop.stop: Two drafts at most, then recruiter writes
loop.why_not_simpler: Readable job text needs prose; the facts themselves come from templates and tables.

steps.what: Explain offer terms and answer doubts in a call

tasks.design: Keep a small maintained table on SharePoint with CAO scales, allowances, shift patterns and site facts per function, owned by C&B. A generator turns it into a vacancy text and a per-vacancy info pack linked from every Recruitee vacancy and invitation mail. An internal answer desk drafts cited replies to remaining candidate mails for the recruiter to send.
tasks.previous_blocker: Pay and shift facts live in the CAO PDF, AFAS and people's heads, so each answer needed a lookup and a fresh mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheap generation of documents from structured tables and cited retrieval over policy text, both quick to build with AI coding.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping the fact table current after CAO changes and indexation; any wrong pay figure has legal and trust costs.
tasks.human_edge: Reading a candidate's doubts in a call and being honest about night shifts, peak season and physical work.

ambition.what: A one-page info pack per vacancy (pay scale, shifts, travel allowance, site, first week) sent with every interview invite.

tasks.altitude: Fewer repeat phone calls; the recruiter spends calls on doubts, not facts, and decides when info packs are good enough to publish.

reach.task: Maintain CAO pay scales and allowances
reach.learn: Own the fact table that feeds candidate information so pay quoted to candidates matches payroll.
Use the same facts as the contract templates to avoid mismatches between offer and contract.

evidence.claim: 57% of hiring leaders use AI for job descriptions.
Recruiter-reviewed emails and job ads need no AI label; a candidate-facing chatbot must say it is AI.
Cited retrieval over policy documents can draft answers for review.

assumptions: Most questions are about pay, shifts, allowances and site, which a fact table covers.
No candidate-facing chatbot is built, so no AI notice is needed.
unknowns: Share of candidate contacts that are fact questions versus doubts.
Languages candidates use, especially for warehouse roles.
Who keeps CAO and site facts current today.
research_questions: Of 50 recent candidate mails and call notes, how many are answered by a fact table?
Do candidates who get an info pack ask fewer questions and drop out less after interview?
Can C&B commit to updating the table within a week of each CAO change?

tasks.short: Shortlist qualified candidates, screen them and recommend hires to hiring managers.

steps.what: Build shortlist from screened candidates per vacancy
Phone screen or interview shortlisted candidates
Write candidate profile and recommendation for the hiring manager

loop.input: recruiter's own scorecard and notes plus candidate facts (no interview recordings)
loop.output: one-page profile per candidate with strengths, gaps and the recruiter's recommendation
loop.check: Every statement must trace to a scorecard field or note; recruiter edits and signs off; no score or ranking added by the model
loop.stop: One draft, one regenerate, then recruiter writes
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning bullet notes into a readable profile needs prose; the facts come straight from fields.

steps.what: Chase manager feedback and interview slots
Discuss recommendation with hiring manager and agree next step

tasks.design: Use Recruitee scorecards as the single record of the recruiter's assessment, and generate the manager profile from them with a bounded drafting step the recruiter approves. A scheduled job reads Recruitee stage dates and nudges managers in Teams when feedback is overdue, with a weekly list of candidates stuck too long. Interviews and the recommendation stay human; no AI notetaker becomes the record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were scattered across mail and Word, and nudging managers took a person watching every pipeline.
tasks.enabler_now: Stage dates are available through the Recruitee API, and profiles can be drafted from structured scorecards in seconds.
tasks.still_hard: Getting managers to act on nudges and to read the profile rather than replace the interview; bias in the recommendation itself.
tasks.human_edge: Judging motivation, reliability and team fit in conversation and standing behind a recommendation to a site manager.

ambition.what: Manager decisions on every shortlisted candidate within three working days, tracked per site.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter stops chasing and spends more time interviewing; they gain a stage-delay view to escalate slow managers to the HRBP with facts.

reach.task: Advise site managers on hiring and team needs
reach.learn: Use stage-delay data per manager to coach on decision speed.
Link recommendations and scorecards to 90-day outcomes to test what predicts success.

evidence.claim: Uniper's hiring agent flagged overdue recruiter and manager tasks; time to contract signature fell 27 days.
Interview summaries become the record; notetakers err and store unlawful questions.
Evaluating candidates is high-risk under the AI Act from 2 December 2027.
The employer stays liable for discrimination by hiring tools.

assumptions: Recruiters will fill Recruitee scorecards consistently.
unknowns: Average days from shortlist to manager decision today.
Whether managers have Recruitee accounts or work by mail.
Works council view on tracking manager response times.
research_questions: How many days does a shortlisted candidate wait for manager feedback today, per site?
Do Teams nudges shorten that wait in a four-week pilot on one site?
Do managers find generated profiles as useful as recruiter-written ones?

tasks.short: Tell applicants where their application stands, by mail and by phone, including rejections.

steps.what: Scan pipelines for candidates who are owed an update
Answer replies asking why or what next

loop.input: candidate reply plus screening note and stage history
loop.output: draft reply in the recruiter's tone
loop.check: Draft may only state reasons recorded in the screening note; recruiter edits and sends
loop.stop: One draft; sensitive replies (complaints, discrimination claims, AVG requests) are flagged and not drafted
loop.why_not_simpler: Replies are free text; templates handle the first message but not follow-ups.

tasks.design: Configure Recruitee to send templated emails on stage changes, with automatic sends for receipt and early-stage rejections after the recruiter's stage move, and recruiter review for post-interview messages. A daily job flags candidates with no contact for five working days in a Teams list. Follow-up replies get a cited draft; post-interview rejections stay a phone call.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates existed but were sent by hand, and nobody saw who had waited too long without a check across all vacancies.
tasks.enabler_now: Stage-triggered email in the ATS plus a simple API job for wait-time flags; AI coding makes the glue cheap.
tasks.still_hard: Writing rejection templates that are kind and specific enough, and keeping stage data accurate so the right mail goes out.
tasks.human_edge: Delivering a rejection after an interview in a way that keeps the candidate willing to apply again or recommend Noordhaven.

ambition.what: Every applicant, including the many early-stage warehouse applicants who now often hear nothing, gets a status within five working days.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter no longer hunts for who is owed an update; they decide the contact standard per stage and spend the time on post-interview calls.

reach.task: Send contract and onboarding documents to new hires
reach.learn: Reuse the stage-triggered mail pattern for pre-boarding messages.

reach.task: Report on candidate experience and drop-off
reach.learn: Add 'days since last contact' as a pipeline metric.

evidence.claim: Recruitee supports email templates sent on pipeline stage moves.
Status updates suit deterministic software with an AI notice where candidate-facing AI is used.
Rejections may not rest solely on automated scoring.

assumptions: Every rejection follows a recruiter's stage move, so no rejection is automated.
Current Recruitee plan includes stage-triggered emails.
unknowns: Share of applicants who now never get a status update.
Current rejection template quality and languages.
Whether candidates complain about silence today.
research_questions: How many applicants in the last quarter waited more than ten working days without contact?
Does Recruitee's built-in automation cover all needed triggers without custom code?
Do candidate replies to automated rejections rise or fall versus hand-sent ones?

role.altitude: The recruiter moves from reading CVs, looking up pay facts and chasing managers to intake, interviews and pushing pipeline speed per site. They gain the right to set must-haves per vacancy with data and to escalate stalled manager decisions to the HRBP.
reach: HR Business Partner: coach site managers on decision speed with stage-delay data
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: own the CAO pay and allowance table that feeds candidate information
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: link screening and recommendations to 90-day retention
Learning and Development Specialist: route hires missing forklift or VCA certificates to training before day one
skills_to_grow: Writing clear, testable must-have requirements with managers
Reviewing AI-extracted facts critically and spotting systematic errors
Reading pipeline stage data and acting on delays
Working within AVG, WOR consent and AI Act duties for hiring tools
role.ambitious_version: One pipeline view per site that shows every vacancy's days per stage, who is waiting on whom, and which must-haves shrink the pool. Every applicant gets a fact check and a status update in days, every candidate gets a clear info pack, and the recruiter's time goes to interviews and to closing the gap between hire and day 90.
